$comment: GAP-HR-SF-09a role-matrix allowlist. Each entry is a KNOWN, currently-accepted drift between hr/layout.tsx's shared HR_ROLES (or a specific /hr, /hr/payroll or /hr/recruitment page's own tighter gate) and the backend route(s) it is responsible for -- discovered by scripts/contract/hr-role-matrix.mjs, a static analyzer that reads both sides live from source on every run. This file does NOT fix any of them (that is GAP-HR-SF-09b's job, gated on SF-20 and the relevant policy decisions per the campaign plan); it only lets the contract test pass today by naming each one, so the test can fail on a genuinely NEW, previously-unknown drift instead of on all 186 already-known ones every time. Never add an entry here to make a NEW drift disappear without asking why it exists first -- that defeats the point of the gate. `match` keys are matched against the analyzer's per-route report exactly: a route's (extraInBackend, extraInWeb, comparator) triple, both arrays compared as sets. GAP-HR-SF-09b (in progress) resolves these entry by entry -- see each removed entry's replacement commit for the resolution, and workRoles.ts's HR_ROLES doc comment for the biggest single cluster (GAP-HR-SF09A-001/002/003/011/012/014, resolved together by one widen).

driftEntries.reason: hr_officer can open the disciplinary list/detail pages (DISCIPLINARY_ROLES admits it) but the 7 highest-stakes actions -- impose penalty, submit-approval, appeal-decision, close, drop, create suspension, revoke suspension -- narrow to hr_admin/super_admin only on the backend. Very plausibly an intentional authorization tier (hr_officer runs routine casework, hr_admin/super_admin signs off on the irreversible/severe steps), but it is a real DISCIPLINARY_ROLES-vs-specific-action mismatch and SF-09b should confirm it is deliberate rather than accidental, since nothing on the web page currently tells an hr_officer which specific buttons will 403 for them.

recruitment/requisition-routes.ts admits a dedicated "hiring_manager" panel role that does not exist anywhere on the web side (not in HR_ROLES, not in any recruitment page gate). Plausibly by design -- ad hoc panel members likely reach requisition approval via a direct/emailed link rather than the general /hr nav -- but if that path doesn't exist yet, a hiring_manager-only account currently has zero way to use these 7 routes through the app.

ai-fraud/routes.ts (AI-assisted fraud detection alerts/scans/risk-scores/recommendations) admits audit_admin, which HR_ROLES doesn't have. Most likely intentional -- this is arguably an audit-service-adjacent surface hosted inside hrms-service -- but audit_admin has no way to reach it via /hr today.

gap-features/performance-dev-routes.ts (goals, development plans) admits a "dept_head" role absent from HR_ROLES and from every page gate. Same shape as GAP-HR-SF09A-005/009 (a participant role with no web-reachable path) -- listed separately since it's a different role name on a different file.

device-trust/routes.ts's block/unblock/policy-update endpoints admit it_admin, absent from HR_ROLES and every page gate. This module's device-trust dashboard route itself (GET /v1/hrms/devices/admin) has NO role check at all -- see GAP-HR-SF09A-019 -- so this whole module's access story needs a look together, not just this one list entry. routeCount corrected 3->5 on 2026-10-01 rebase onto current main: device-trust/routes.ts grew two more it_admin-gated endpoints (now 5 call sites of the identical requireRole(["hr_admin","it_admin","super_admin"]) pattern at lines 203/255/286/303/329) since this entry was last written; same reasoning applies to all five.

recruitment/interview-scoring-routes.ts admits a dedicated "interviewer" panel role, same shape as GAP-HR-SF09A-005 (hiring_manager) and GAP-HR-SF09A-007 (dept_head) -- three different ad hoc recruitment-panel roles, none reachable via /hr nav today.

Same action-tiering shape as GAP-HR-SF09A-004: APAR_ROLES admits employee/manager to view and to work their own self-appraisal/reporting/reviewing/accept/representation steps, but raw create (POST /v1/hrms/apar) and finalise narrow to hr_admin/hr_officer/super_admin on the backend -- plausibly intentional, worth SF-09b's explicit confirmation.

POST /v1/hrms/declarations/:declId/revoke (disciplinary/coi-routes.ts, Conflict-of-Interest declarations) admits a "vigilance_officer" role. This is UNRELATED to the /hr/vigilance page (that page covers a different backend concept, gap-features.ts's "vigilance cases", and its own VIGILANCE_ROLES cleanly matches gap-features.ts already -- see hr-role-matrix.json). "vigilance_officer" itself appears nowhere else in either service and has no web-side representation anywhere (not HR_ROLES, not any page gate, not even the /hr/vigilance page's own list) -- if this role is meant to have any web-facing capability, it currently has none at all.

GET /v1/hrms/work-summaries accepts "employee" (self-service: an employee viewing their own work summary), but the web page's WORK_SUMMARY_ROLES omits employee entirely -- so a plain employee is shown "Access Restricted" by hr/work-summary/page.tsx before the backend call that would have actually worked for them ever runs. Same shape as this codebase's own already-fixed salary-slip employee-access bug (see the payroll/slips/[id] comment history) -- a strong candidate for SF-09b to fix first.

Deliberate, intentional narrowing, not a bug: the published decision packet's own recommendation for GAP-HR-ICC-02 is "identity only through a dedicated icc_member-only detail route, audited -- the statutory default, not really optional." GET /v1/hrms/icc/complaints/:id is the ONLY route that ever returns complainantId/respondentId (POSH Act 2013 s.16) -- unlike the list route (GET /v1/hrms/icc/complaints, which correctly matches page:icc's ICC_ROLES: hr_admin/super_admin/icc_member), this detail route is icc_member-ONLY by design, excluding hr_admin/super_admin. A chairing hr_admin needs the icc_member role granted to them (a role-assignment decision, out of this fix's scope), not a code-level bypass on the one route that exposes identity. The analyzer maps this route to the page's shared ICC_ROLES comparator by file, not by exact path, so this drift is expected to persist until the analyzer grows a per-route-path comparator for icc-routes.ts's two GET routes.

Same action-tiering shape as GAP-HR-SF09A-004/010: ADVANCE_ROLES admits manager/officer (and now also employee) to view and request salary advances, but PATCH .../approve and PATCH .../reject narrow to finance_admin/hr_admin/hr_officer/super_admin on the backend -- an approval/rejection step correctly excluding the requester's own tier, most likely intentional. Corrected on 2026-10-01's rebase onto current main: extraInWeb was [manager,officer] (routeCount 1, approve only); employee was added to ADVANCE_ROLES by an unrelated already-merged change since this entry was first written, and reject carries the identical backend role list to approve -- both now extraInWeb=[employee,manager,officer], routeCount 2. Caught only because this rebase re-ran the analyzer against current main, same as GAP-HR-SF-16/GAP-HR-SF09A-019's precedent.

NOT a real drift -- a confirmed analyzer false positive, found during the 2026-10-01 GAP-HR-SF-09b rebase. leave-policies/page.tsx imports LEAVE_POLICY_ADMIN_ROLES via the "@/lib/auth/workRoles" path alias; hr-role-matrix.mjs's getFileImports() only follows relative ("./", "../") import specifiers (`if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;`), so it never resolves this page's own gate, resolvePageConst() falls back to `{roles: null}`, and main()'s `comparatorRoles = resolved.roles ?? []` silently turns that into an EMPTY array instead of surfacing an error -- making every one of these 4 routes' real roles look like an unexplained mismatch. The real LEAVE_POLICY_ADMIN_ROLES (apps/web/src/lib/auth/workRoles.ts) is exactly ["hr_admin", "super_admin", "tenant_admin", "platform_admin"] -- an EXACT match with these 4 backend routes' own role list (leave/policy-admin-routes.ts's HR_ADMIN_ROLES), confirmed by direct source comparison, not assumed. Allowlisted as a known-false-positive rather than fixed here since the fix (path-alias resolution in getFileImports) is shared-tooling scope beyond this rebase; flagged separately as a follow-up rather than silently left unexplained.

noRoleCheckEntries.reason: Routes with no requireRole/requirePermissionKey call found at all -- any authenticated caller of ANY role reaches them (this is a materially different, more serious class of finding than a role-list drift, since it means the backend enforces no HR-role boundary whatsoever, not just a different one than the web expects). Sub-groups: (1) the "social" module -- kudos, kudos/feed, announcements, travel-requests, expenses(!), device registration, org chart, pulse-surveys, goals, leaderboard, AI assistant (19 routes across social/routes.ts + social/pulse-routes.ts). (2) gpf/routes.ts's four money-movement endpoints (subscription/advance/withdrawal/refund) -- no role check at all on PF transactions. (3) device-trust/routes.ts's admin dashboard, per-device activity log and policy GET routes (the /me ones are correctly excluded as self-service, see hr-role-matrix.mjs's OUT_OF_SCOPE_PATTERNS). (4) deputation/routes.ts's repatriate/cancel actions. (5) payroll-service's form16-verify POST route. GAP-HR-SF-09b (this PR) deliberately does NOT touch this bucket -- these are missing-guard security exposures, not role-list drifts, and fixing them means choosing what role SHOULD gate each one (a product/security decision), not reconciling two existing gates the way every driftEntries item above does; several (the money-movement gpf endpoints especially) deserve a dedicated security-flagged fix wave the same way GAP-HR-SF-16 got, not a role-matrix side-fix. routeCount corrected 32->30: GET /v1/hrms/social/feed and GET /v1/hrms/birthdays/today both now carry a real role check (confirmed via `git show HEAD:scripts/contract/hr-role-matrix.json` vs a live re-run) -- GAP-HR-SF-16 (self-scoping leak fix) landed on origin/main after this file's 2026-09-29 snapshot and evidently covered both in social/routes.ts's module-wide cleanup; unrelated to GAP-HR-SF-09b's own changes, caught only because this PR re-ran the analyzer against current main. None of the remaining 30 are fixed by this PR. routeCount further corrected 30->28 on 2026-10-01 (rebase onto current main, ~68 commits after this entry's prior 2026-09-29 correction): GET /v1/hrms/devices/admin and GET /v1/hrms/devices/:deviceId/activity (sub-group 3) now both carry a real role check (requireRole(ctx, ["hr_admin","it_admin","super_admin"])), landing alongside the two new it_admin routes GAP-HR-SF09A-008 now also tracks -- confirmed via `git show 4f135eaa9:scripts/contract/hr-role-matrix.json` vs a live re-run, same method used for the prior correction. Unrelated to GAP-HR-SF-09b's own changes. Remaining 28: device-trust's GET /v1/hrms/devices/policy and GET /v1/hrms/devices/me are still unguarded in that sub-group.

dynamicEntries.reason: recruitment/offer-routes.ts's approve/return actions and recruitment/requisition-routes.ts's approve/return actions each call requireRole(ctx, [role, "super_admin"]) where `role` is a runtime-computed value (the specific approval-chain role for that requisition/offer's current stage), not a static list this analyzer -- or any purely static analyzer -- can resolve. Not a defect; recorded so the allowlist doesn't have to silently swallow "errors" on every future re-run, and so a human auditing approval-chain authorization knows to look at these 4 call sites directly rather than trusting this matrix for them. A 5th call site, service-book/pdf-routes.ts:39's requireRole(ctx, READER_ROLES), was added to this count on 2026-10-01 during a rebase onto current main -- but unlike the four above, its role list IS fully static (see this entry's full note in the rebase record); it only resolves as DYNAMIC because of a separate analyzer import-resolution bug (`.js` specifier vs the real `.ts` file), tracked as a follow-up rather than fixed in this change.

noBackendRouteFound.reason: No route in services/hrms-service or services/payroll-service serves this page (surveyed: all 783 routes across both services). "location_user"/"location_admin" do not appear anywhere in either service's role vocabulary. A sibling, non-hr-prefixed page (apps/web/src/app/(app)/locations/maps/page.tsx) and a large, wholly separate services/location-service (cadastral, geocoding, geofence, hierarchy, land-records, routing, etc.) exist in this repo -- location-service was NOT surveyed by this analyzer (out of the named scope: it is a general-purpose GIS platform service, not HR/payroll/recruitment-adjacent). Needs out-of-band verification: either hr/locations calls location-service under a path this analyzer wouldn't recognize as HR's, or this create form has no live backend at all. Excluded from the route-level allowlist above since there is no in-scope route to compare against.
